Candidates are ordered by decreasing retrieval similarity. This ordering is a useful prior, not a guarantee.
Use the peak evidence and structural compatibility; theoretical and experimental Raman spectra may differ.
Do not invent, modify, or combine candidates. Even when uncertain, choose the best available candidate.
End your response with these fields:

## Full Rule Details (for reference)

- **GFQ-003** [DEFINITIVE] C-H stretching: ~2900-3100 cm⁻¹; C-H bending: ~1300-1500 cm⁻¹ [source: nakamoto2008infrared]
- **GFQ-039** [DEFINITIVE] CH₄: ν₁ 2917, ν₂ 1534, ν₃ 3019, ν₄ 1306 cm⁻¹. SiH₄: ν₁ 2180, ν₂ 970, ν₃ 2183, ν₄ 910 cm⁻¹. GeH₄: ν₁ 2106, ν₂ 931, ν₃ 2114, ν₄ 819 cm⁻¹ [source: nakamoto2008infrared]
- **GFQ-015** [EXPERIMENTALLY_VERIFIED] Fullerene C₆₀ characteristic modes: IR-active at 1428, 1182, 577, 527 cm⁻¹; Raman-active pentagonal pinching mode (A_g) at 1469 cm⁻¹, radial breathing (A_g) at 496 cm⁻¹ [source: nakamoto2008infrared]
- **SEL-010** [EXPERIMENTALLY_VERIFIED] Icosahedral C₆₀ (Ih): only 4 F₁u vibrations are IR-active; only 2 A_g and 8 H_g vibrations are Raman-active. Mutual exclusion rule holds [source: nakamoto2008infrared]
- **SPC-010** [EXPERIMENTALLY_VERIFIED] Isotopic fine structure in C₆₀: natural ¹³C (1.11%) gives 51% ¹²C₆₀, 35% ¹²C₅₉¹³C, 11% ¹²C₅₈¹³C₂. The pentagonal pinching A_g mode splits into 1471, 1470, 1469 cm⁻¹ peaks [source: nakamoto2008infrared]
- **GFQ-010** [HIGH] C≡C (triple bond) stretching: ~1700-2200 cm⁻¹ (C₂: ~1757 cm⁻¹ matrix); C=C (double): ~1500-1680 cm⁻¹; C-C (single): ~1000-1300 cm⁻¹ [source: nakamoto2008infrared]
- **GFQ-064** [HIGH] Hydrogen bifluoride [F-H-F]⁻: linear symmetric. ν₃(asym stretch) ~1450, ν₂(bend) ~1233, ν₁(sym stretch) ~596-603 cm⁻¹. [F-H-Cl]⁻ type I (asym): ν₃ ~2500, type II (sym): ν₃ ~933 cm⁻¹ [source: nakamoto2008infrared]
- **GFQ-049** [HIGH] Boron hydrides: terminal ν(BH) ~2600-2500, bridging ν(B-H-B) ~2200-2100 cm⁻¹. ν(Ga-H) terminal ~2005-1982, bridging ~1435-1315. ν(B-H) in NH₃BH₃ ~2340 cm⁻¹ [source: nakamoto2008infrared]
- **GEO-001** [HIGH] Distinguishing linear vs bent XY₂: ν₁ is IR-inactive for linear (D∞h) but IR-active for bent (C2v). In practice, many bent molecules have bond angles 95-170° [source: nakamoto2008infrared]
- **GEO-002** [DEFINITIVE] Distinguishing pyramidal (C3v) vs planar (D3h) XY₃: pyramidal shows 2 stretching bands (ν₁ A₁ + ν₃ E) in IR; planar shows 1 stretching band (ν₃ E′) in IR [source: nakamoto2008infrared]
- **GEO-003** [HIGH] Distinguishing trigonal-bipyramidal (D3h) vs tetragonal-pyramidal (C4v) XY₅: TBP has 2 IR-active stretches; TP has 3 IR-active stretches [source: nakamoto2008infrared]
- **GEO-004** [HIGH] Bond angle calculation in YXY from isotopic frequency ratio: use ν₃/ν₃′ ratio with isotopic substitution at X [source: nakamoto2008infrared]
- **GEO-005** [HIGH] For X₂Y₄ (ethane-like) molecules: trans (C2h) shows 6 IR fundamentals, gauche (C2) shows 12 IR fundamentals [source: nakamoto2008infrared]
- **GEO-006** [HIGH] For X₂Y₄ (B₂X₄-type) molecules: D2h (planar) vs D2d (staggered) distinguished by number of IR fundamentals: 8 for D2, 5 for D2d [source: nakamoto2008infrared]
- **GEO-008** [DEFINITIVE] Cis/trans isomer distinction in octahedral XY₄Z₂: trans (D4h) gives 3 XY stretches (A1g+B1g+Eu) with Eu IR-active only; cis (C2v) gives 4 XY stretches (2A1+B1+B2) all IR+Raman active [source: nakamoto2008infrared]
- **GEO-009** [HIGH] Distinction between cis/trans isomers in X₂Y₂ molecules: cis (C2v) vs trans (C2h). ν₆ vibration is IR-inactive and Raman-depolarized in planar but IR-active and Raman-polarized in nonplanar [source: nakamoto2008infrared]
- **GEO-010** [HIGH] Planar (D2h) vs twisted (D2) X₂H₄: D2h has IR/Raman mutual exclusion; D2 (nonplanar) does not [source: nakamoto2008infrared]
- **GEO-011** [HIGH] D3h (staggered) vs D3h′ (eclipsed) for ethane-like X₂Y₆: D3d has E_u IR-active + E_g Raman-active; D3h has E′ both IR and Raman active [source: nakamoto2008infrared]
- **GEO-012** [EXPERIMENTALLY_VERIFIED] Small silicon clusters Siₙ: counting Raman-active fundamentals identifies geometry (e.g., Si₄ planar rhombus D2h: 3 Raman; Si₆ distorted octahedron D4h: 5 Raman; Si₇ pentagonal bipyramid D5h: 5 Raman) [source: nakamoto2008infrared]
- **GEO-013** [HIGH] Trigonal-bipyramidal structure has stronger equatorial bonds than axial bonds (confirmed by force constant calculations). Tetragonal-pyramidal has stronger axial bond [source: nakamoto2008infrared]
- **GEO-015** [EXPERIMENTALLY_VERIFIED] Endohedral fullerene symmetry: violation of mutual exclusion rule and more IR/Raman bands than predicted for Ih symmetry indicates lowering due to metal-cage interaction [source: nakamoto2008infrared]
- **SUB-002** [HIGH] Mixed halogen systems: stretching frequencies are additive and characteristic. For mixed complexes, ratios ν(MBr)/ν(MCl) ≈ 0.76 and ν(MI)/ν(MCl) ≈ 0.62 for ν₃ [source: nakamoto2008infrared]
- **SUB-004** [HIGH] Terminal vs bridging M-X stretching: terminal frequencies are higher than bridging frequencies. Ratio ν(bridge)/ν(terminal) ranges from 0.74 to 0.61 [source: nakamoto2008infrared]
- **CHG-003** [HIGH] For tetrahedral oxoanions MO₄ⁿ⁻: ν₁/ν₃ ratio increases with (1) increasing negative charge for same central atom, (2) increasing mass of central atom for same charge, (3) increasing negative charge for isoelectronic ions [source: nakamoto2008infrared]
- **CHG-004** [DEFINITIVE] Removing bonding electrons → frequency decrease; removing antibonding electrons → frequency increase (diatomics) [source: nakamoto2008infrared]
- **CHG-005** [HIGH] For NH₄⁺ in ammonium halides: ν(NH₄⁺) decreases and δ(NH₄⁺) increases as N-H···X hydrogen bond weakens in order X = F > Cl > Br > I [source: nakamoto2008infrared]
